limitations: No measured local cavity/source/noise envelope is certified here.
Finite Gaussian covariance results assume their declared texture and baseline covariance.
The raw-noise oracle theorem is general; the scenario tables use a finite spectral model, not qualified raw telemetry.
Dynamic far-field extrapolation remains an explicit input assumption.
Sampled frequency/direction results do not exclude narrow unsampled resonances or other excitations.
The statistical target is illustrative; failing it does not prove all archaeological utility is zero.

depth_oracle.status: P2-29 solver kernels; the class admits rooms spread 15 m down (dilute superposition checked)

finding: Loose but simple, and with the common background included, the finite certificate caps any processor's detection rate at 5.0172% at 5% false alarms under the regional microseism envelope (detection minus false alarm at most 1.72e-04; P2-25's tighter bound, reference covariance I: 1.3e-09). Every static row excludes 95% at 5%. Of P2-26's dynamic rows the thin-roof room under a truck-level harmonic is the open one: at most 89.1% at 5%, and no longer excluded if its phase is 11% larger. An arbitrary phase modulation within the background envelope on 52,600 pixels is capped at 9.55%; on the whole image the certificate is uninformative. Depth: P2-29's spread rooms 15 m down leave 71% of a room 30 m down's mark unmatched, so where detection just reaches 95% at 5% Theorem E's floor on any method's mean depth error between the two is only 1.8 m of their 15 m separation: in this model the mark's shape carries depth.
